checkers.description: Exact rational feasibility and upper certificate for the unchanged Li–Yang Theorem 4.1 LP. Arithmetic evidence only.

objectives.name: gate_coefficient
objectives.semantics: First transport coordinate of the jointly accepted bound.json declaration. Finite c>0 is exact; an endpoint uses positive_infinity and has no native numeric tuple. The full expression metric is authoritative.

objectives.name: gate_exponent
objectives.semantics: Second transport coordinate of the SAME jointly accepted theorem. Finite rational p>=1; a global endpoint uses positive_infinity only as a transport placeholder. Never interpret it as n^infinity.
objectives.unit: power of actual input length n

scoring.instructions: Apply the joint coefficient/exponent contract in rules.md. Both source claims must state and prove the same complete bound.json declaration and have identical evidence. Review the entire quantified guarantee, including any v2 eventual_lower_bound remainder, and its projection for one fixed eligible family. Explicit remainder means there exists N such that for every integer n>=N, C(n)>=L(n)-sum(terms(n)); big_o means there exist K>0 and N such that for every integer n>=N, C(n)>=L(n)-K*n^a*(log2 n)^b*(log2 log2 n)^d. A liminf or little-o leading statement alone never establishes a particular remainder, even with the same finite scores. Do not infer a remainder from prose, floats, or comparison hints. Atomic validity is mandatory. Endpoint score fields are transport only, not numerical infinite exponents. Zero coefficient earns no exponent. Return scores:null.

validity.instructions: Apply rules.md to every original claim and its evidence. The same fixed uniform NP family must work for all coefficients, all exponents in a global theorem, and all sufficiently large actual integer lengths. Unsupported conditions, family swaps, model changes, or larger projected guarantees invalidate the main claim. No scientific acceptance follows from a schema or LP checker pass.
